title: Sequencer jitter handoff and variability capture - 2026-11-17
content:
Sync objective: capture the current state of the 'sequencer jitter' investigation, summarize reproducible steps, enumerate what we tried in the lab yesterday, and assign next actions. This doc is a living capture from the 2026-11-17 perf sync (15:00 PT).

Summary (one-liner):
- Intermittent p99 spikes and throughput plateau observed when running multi-model ensemble workloads at sustained QPS > 600 on Dedicated pools; early signal points to sequencing edge cases where request interleaving and backpressure produce micro-jitter that cascades into tail events.

Observed timeline and trigger:
- 2026-11-15: First customer report (support case TCK-3109) showing periodic 2–4s p99 spikes during high-concurrency inference.
- 2026-11-16 morning: Shadow-run of ensemble-3 (resnet+transformer reranker) reproduced plateau at ~620 QPS. p50 stable, p95 up ~30%, p99 bursts up to 2.1s.
- 2026-11-16 evening: Local lab runs with debug tracing enabled captured sequencer handoff events aligned with kernel scheduling preemption.

Reproduction steps used in lab (exact commands):
- traffic generator: ./tools/traffic-gen --profile ensemble-3 --qps 650 --concurrency 120 --duration 30m --payload-size 1kb
- docker image: serving-runtime:main-20261114-debug
- sequencer tracing: SRT_TRACE=sequencer_verbose ./serve --config test/ensemble-3.yaml
- collection: /tmp/trace-$(date +%s).pb.gz (we uploaded sample to Confluence link above)

Key metric snapshot (baseline vs problematic run):
- Baseline (no ensemble, single-model): p50=18ms, p95=42ms, p99=89ms, throughput stable at target QPS.
- Problematic (ensemble-3, qps=650): p50=22ms, p95=63ms (+50%), p99=2100ms (+~2300%), throughput plateau at 610–630 QPS.
- CPU/GPU: GPUs saturated at 70–75% (expected); host CPU occasional spike to 95% coincident with p99 windows.

Traces & artifacts we examined:
- Sample trace #A (trace id 20261116-0543): shows sequencer thread 1 performing handoff, then waiting on queue drain for ~300–400ms before next batch vectorization step.
- Kernel schedule logs: several preemptions at 15–20ms intervals that align with handoff boundaries.
- Shadow-run diffs: when we disabled cross-request KV cache prefetch (feature flag kv-prefetch=false) tail reduced by ~35%.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Sequencer handoff aligns poorly with OS scheduler quantum under certain concurrency shapes -> micro-pauses aggregate into tail spikes. Evidence: host CPU preempt trace and 15–20ms gaps.
2) Cross-request KV prefetching introduces stalls when memory bandwidth contention occurs, coupling with sequencer timing to produce large waits. Evidence: disabling kv-prefetch reduced tail.
3) Backpressure propagation from a slow downstream model in the ensemble leads to head-of-line blocking inside the sequencer queue. Evidence: one model occasionally has 3x variance in exec time during the problematic windows.

Experiments run (yesterday):
- E1: Increase sequencer worker threads by +2 (from 8 -> 10) while keeping QPS constant. Result: minor p50 improvement, no p99 improvement.
- E2: Pin sequencer threads to isolated CPUs (cpuset) to reduce scheduler noise. Result: p99 decreased from 2.1s -> 1.3s during 30m run, throughput improved to 640 QPS.
- E3: Toggle kv-prefetch=false. Result: p99 decreased to ~1.0s and throughput climbed to 655 QPS; memory bandwidth usage dropped ~18%.
- E4: Introduced small jitter randomizer in sequencer handoff (add 1–3ms sleep) to avoid pathological alignment. Result: p99 lowered modestly but added steady latency increase to p50 (~+3ms).

Conclusions so far:
- Best signal points to interaction of CPU scheduling + kv-prefetch memory contention. Isolating sequencer threads (cpuset) + disabling kv-prefetch gave the largest wins together.
- Workaround for impacted customers: deploy cpuset isolation and disable kv-prefetch on Dedicated pools that host ensembles until a permanent fix is implemented.

Open questions / unknowns:
- Why does disabling kv-prefetch have such a large effect only under ensemble workloads and not single-model runs? Could prefetching pattern be thrashing shared caches only when multiple models are invoked per request?
- Do different kernel versions (driver/kernel) affect scheduling behavior? We saw minor differences between node images node-2026-10-02 and node-2026-10-28. Need broader test matrix.
- Are there hardware-specific amplifiers (e.g., NUMA placement, NIC interrupts) that make some fleets worse? Customer's Dedicated pool is on heterogeneous hosts.

Short-term action items (owners & ETA):
- A1: Roll temporary mitigation to staging dedicated pool: cpuset for sequencer + kv-prefetch=false (owner: Owen Brooks, ETA: 2026-11-18).
- A2: Expand lab matrix to include kernel versions and NUMA configs (owner: Lina Gomez, ETA: 2026-11-20). Add test permutations for node images node-2026-09, node-2026-10-02, node-2026-10-28.
- A3: Add more trace points around KV prefetch (owner: Marcus Li, ETA: 2026-11-19). Goal: capture memory bandwidth counters and prefetch queue latency.
- A4: Customer comms draft for impacted accounts with mitigations and expected timeline (owner: Priya Shah, ETA: 2026-11-18).
- A5: Spike PR to make sequencer handoff resilient: option for adaptive handoff (owner: Nina Patel, ETA: spike by 2026-11-24, PR target 4829 reference).

Longer-term proposals (for design doc):
- Move sequencer to a soft real-time scheduling domain on hosts that support it (requires SRE and infra agreement).
- Rework kv-prefetch to be bandwidth-aware (adaptive rate limit based on mem BW telemetry).
- Consider per-ensemble scheduling lanes so slow models do not block others.

Meeting notes / conversational captures:
- Owen: "the cpuset isolation was surprisingly effective; suggests co-scheduling noise is a big factor."
- Lina: "we need to be careful we don't overfit to the one customer's workload shape — broaden the workload shapes in lab."
- Marcus: "kernel/driver differences might explain fleet variance; already filed JIRA-PERF-9180 to track node image tests."

Notes to self / TODOs:
- Upload the 3 representative trace pb.gz files to Confluence and link from the Jira ticket.
- Add a short dashboard tile showing sequencer thread run queue length sampled at 100ms resolution.

Appendix (quick debug artefacts):
- Representative commands used to collect perf counters:
  - perf stat -e cache-misses,cycles -I 1000 -p <sequencer-pid>
  - pidstat -h 1 -p <sequencer-pid>
- Quick grep pattern for handoff gaps in tracing logs: grep -n "handoff_complete" trace-*.log | awk -F":" '{print $1, $3}'

If you're taking an action above, please add a short status update in the Jira ticket and drop a note in #perf-standup thread. We'll reconvene next sync (2026-11-19, 15:00 PT) with lab matrix results and any customer-impact rollouts.

Unresolved: who on infra can provision a test fleet with consistent CPU topology? Lina to escalate to infra channel and tag infra-eng.
